name: 051_retail_crowd_fade_tf240
hypothesis: PLAN.md section 14, idea M2 (new data: the all-accounts long/short ratio, mostly retail). When the account ratio is far above its own recent range, many small accounts are long with leverage; their stops and liquidations sit below price, and the funding they pay makes the position costly to hold, so the crowded side unwinds over the next days. Fade it: the log ratio's z-score (last 720 bars) crosses above +z -> short; crosses below -z (the crowd is unusually short) -> long. Counterparty: late retail positioning, the same crowd that funding_extreme tried to read through funding (Exp 016, REJECT), measured here directly by account counts instead of by price of carry. In a falling market retail typically buys the dip, so the ratio rises while price falls and this goes short with the trend; that is the case it should win. Held 2-6 days. Grid: how extreme the crowd must be, and the hold. [Timeframe variant of 051_retail_crowd_fade, 60m -> 240m, mode chart: same bar counts and ATR multiples, hold x4, pct stop x2.000.]
